topology_reasoning.device: A symmetric, contra-oriented pair of S-bent strip waveguides forming a long parallel directional-coupler interaction region.
topology_reasoning.operation: The two ports on each side are vertically separated. Each guide moves inward through an S-bend, co-propagates beside the other guide in the central straight section for power transfer, then S-bends back outward to the opposite-side port separation.
observations_from_image: The 120 um by 4 um calibrated footprint contains two disconnected black tracks on one material layer.
Both tracks have approximately constant width, horizontal access sections, mirrored S-bends, and a long central parallel run.
The central runs are closely spaced, so their gap and overlap length are the coupling-defining geometry.

iteration_history.change_made: Initial primitive reconstruction: two 0.30 um cosine S-bend paths, 12.5 um bends, 70 um interaction length. The diff showed both bends completed too early.
Lengthened the bends to 15.5 um and shortened the parallel interaction to 58 um, based on calibrated left/right bend extents.
Mapped the observed S-bend centerline profile into a parametric GF Path, fitted distinct guide widths, and corrected the central guide separation.
Used separate left/right and upper/lower centerline profiles and fitted the slight port-height asymmetry visible in the raster.
Refined sampled bend-progress values from centerline measurements; the remaining mismatch is the source's non-parametric stroke asymmetry.

Added path-derived arm-length reporting and made the upper interaction length independently tunable for the required geometric knob-response proof; flattened the final primitive assembly so its layer area is independently measurable.
